issue_context.title: /api/v1/directory returning 500 on Mastodon 4.1.11
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce the problem

On a Mastodon 4.1.11 instance:

1. Go to `your-domain.tld/directory` on a browser. A `GET` request is made to `/api/v1/directory?order=active&local=false&limit=20`
2. Check the mastodon-web logs and the database logs


### Expected behaviour

The `/directory` page shows some profiles

### Actual behaviour

The `/directory` page loads, but doesn't show any profile

### Detailed description

The API call to `/api/v1/directory?order=active&local=false&limit=20` gives a `500` error

mastodon-web logs:

LINE 1: ... NULL AND "accounts"."discoverable" = $2 ORDER BY last_statu...

### Mastodon instance

https://mastodon.libre-entreprise.com

### Mastodon version

v4.1.11

### Technical details

Mastodon running with Docker, using official image
comments: @ClearlyClaire did we forgot to backport a fix here?

I do remember us simplifying the discovery queries, I'll look into that.

We changed something related in #27306, which is in both 4.2.3 and 4.1.11.
Seems like the scope change in #26842 (<https://github.com/mastodon/mastodon/pull/26842/commits/6684b1621a42d072ce4d8ac62dcccef1c248b2f2>) should fix it.
Fixed by #28412, will be in 4.1.12, or you can update to the `stable-4.1` branch.

I have the same issue on 3.5.15 and 3.5.16 (and possibly previous 3.5.X but I didn't notice)

It also breaks the `/explore` page.

Technically 3.5.X is not end-of-life until... tomorrow ;)
I plan to upgrade very soon.
In the meantime, I can confirm that backporting #28412 also fixes the issue in stable-3.5

review_comments: This means that accounts that don't yet have an `account_stat` row (e.g. 0 posts, following, followers) will not be returned. That is actually probably fine in practice, but it is different, and I'm not really sure how this would fix a HTTP 500 error because of an ambigous column.

Because of another recent backported change (#27306), the generated SQL was a mess with two joins on `account_stat`, which caused the ambiguous query error. This PR fixes it. It's true that this makes accounts with 0 (known) posts or followers not appear, but I think this is fine in the profile directory.
